comparisons.peer_topic: Status of Legal Proceedings and Potential Losses
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, AMD had no material legal proceedings, though it is involved in various actions arising in the normal course of business. Management believes that any reasonably possible losses, individually or in aggregate, will not have a material adverse effect on the company's financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose their status regarding legal proceedings in Item 8. Intel reports a specific, material patent infringement case (VLSI) with a significant jury award and pending license defense, whereas AMD discloses that it had no material legal proceedings as of its fiscal year-end, though it is involved in various routine actions. The key difference is the presence of a specific, high-stakes litigation event in Intel's disclosures versus a general statement of no material proceedings for AMD.

sentences.text: ▪The third Texas case went to trial in November 2022, with VLSI asserting one remaining patent. The jury found the patent valid and infringed, and awarded VLSI approximately $949 million in damages, plus interest and a running royalty. The court has not yet entered final judgment. In February 2023, we filed motions for a new trial and for judgment as a matter of law notwithstanding the verdict on various grounds. Further appeals are possible. In April 2024, Intel moved to add the defense that it is licensed to VLSI's patents, and the court granted Intel's motion that same month. Trial on the license defense has been set for May 2025.
As of December 28, 2024, there were no material legal proceedings.

With respect to these matters, based on management's current knowledge, the Company believes that the amount or range of reasonably possible loss, if any, will not, either individually or in the aggregate, have a material adverse effect on the Company's financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.

comparisons.peer_topic: Netlist E.D. Tex. litigation verdict and PTAB proceedings
comparisons.peer_summary: In Netlist's E.D. Tex. litigation, a jury found Micron liable for infringing two patents, awarding $425 million and $20 million in damages, respectively; Micron intends to appeal, though the PTAB found the asserted claims unpatentable.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron (MU) disclose specific, high-value patent infringement litigation outcomes in their Item 8 notes. Intel's disclosure concerns the VLSI case where a jury awarded approximately $949 million, with a license defense trial set for 2025. Micron's disclosure concerns the Netlist case where a jury awarded $425 million and $20 million, with Micron appealing the verdict. Both companies are defendants in significant patent infringement suits in the Eastern District of Texas with substantial jury awards and active post-trial legal processes (appeals or license defense trials).

sentences.text: ▪The third Texas case went to trial in November 2022, with VLSI asserting one remaining patent. The jury found the patent valid and infringed, and awarded VLSI approximately $949 million in damages, plus interest and a running royalty. The court has not yet entered final judgment. In February 2023, we filed motions for a new trial and for judgment as a matter of law notwithstanding the verdict on various grounds. Further appeals are possible. In April 2024, Intel moved to add the defense that it is licensed to VLSI's patents, and the court granted Intel's motion that same month. Trial on the license defense has been set for May 2025.

On May 23, 2024, following a four-day trial regarding the second complaint filed by Netlist in the E.D. Tex., a jury rendered a verdict that Micron's memory modules infringe two asserted patents - U.S. Patent No. 7,619,912 ("the '912 patent") and U.S. Patent No. 11,093,417 ("the '417 patent") - and found that Micron should pay $425 million for infringement of the '912 patent and $20 million for infringement of the '417 patent.

On April 17, 2024, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board ("PTAB") of the United States Patent and Trademark Office ("USPTO") issued a final written decision ("FWD") finding unpatentable the sole asserted claim of the '912 patent.

comparisons.peer_topic: In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation Status
comparisons.peer_summary: The Ninth Circuit affirmed in part and reversed in part the dismissal of the securities class action on August 25, 2023; NVIDIA obtained a stay of the mandate on December 5, 2023, pending its petition for certiorari to the Supreme Court, with a filing deadline of March 4, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA (NVDA) disclose significant pending legal proceedings in Item 8, though the nature of the litigation differs. Intel is involved in a patent infringement case with a specific damages award and pending license defense. NVIDIA is involved in a securities class action that has advanced through appellate courts (Ninth Circuit) and is pending further review. Both disclosures highlight complex, long-running legal matters with uncertain outcomes, but Intel's is IP-focused while NVIDIA's is securities-focused.

sentences.text: ▪The third Texas case went to trial in November 2022, with VLSI asserting one remaining patent. The jury found the patent valid and infringed, and awarded VLSI approximately $949 million in damages, plus interest and a running royalty. The court has not yet entered final judgment. In February 2023, we filed motions for a new trial and for judgment as a matter of law notwithstanding the verdict on various grounds. Further appeals are possible. In April 2024, Intel moved to add the defense that it is licensed to VLSI's patents, and the court granted Intel's motion that same month. Trial on the license defense has been set for May 2025.

On August 25, 2023, a majority of a three-judge Ninth Circuit panel affirmed in part and reversed in part the district court's dismissal of the case, with a third judge dissenting on the basis that the district court did not err in dismissing the case.

On November 15, 2023, the Ninth Circuit denied NVIDIA's petition for rehearing en banc of the Ninth Circuit panel's majority decision to reverse in part the dismissal of the case, which NVIDIA had filed on October 10, 2023.
